notes.title: Winter Survival just got Major Update! 👀
notes.notes: [h1]Hey, survivors! ❄️[/h1][p][/p][p]Welcome to another [b]major update for Winter Survival[/b]. After a series of episodes where we’ve been teasing a little bit of what we’ve been working on for the past few months, it's high time to finally share it with our beloved community. We’ve rolled out a brand-new update packed with [b]reworks, improvements, and bug fixes[/b] to make your survival experience smoother, more balanced, and more immersive. Stick with me till the end, as we might have something that you’d definitely want to keep an eye out on 👀[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/f99dab292d8314b59a37f55c8b610a199e6d700b.png"][/img][/p][p]Due to fundamental changes in the game’s questline and various other data, we regret to announce that old save files are no longer compatible after this update (16th of September, 2025). [/p][p]If you want to continue your old playthrough, please make sure to use the “legacy” branch.[/p][p]More information can be found in the pinned thread via Steam discussions. You can also proceed directly to that thread by clicking [url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/1394960/discussions/0/572642335441059103/"]this link[/url] If you want to continue your playthrough on your old saves, it might be worth to have some sort of a backup of your old saves. Check [url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/1394960/discussions/0/572642335441059300/"]this link[/url] to see how to do it properly. [/p][p]When starting the game, there is a new screen that will open up - Shader Compilation Screen. This will attempt to precompile all shaders in the game for your hardware so that the game can run smoothly when being played, rather than compiling them on the go (which can be a cause of hitches). The visual representation of this widget is temporary.[/p][p]The compilation of shaders is very resource-intensive on the hardware, so if you are getting repeated crashes on this, please let us know your computer specs here or on Discord - CPU, GPU, and Hard Disk that you are installing the game on as it can help us remove these issues before full release of the game, or finding alternative solutions for these cases. Restarting a game may help with some of the issues.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Major Reworks & Improvements 🛠️[/b][/h2][p][i][b]Note:[/b] These patch notes highlight a selection of fixes and improvements. They are not exhaustive. Many systems were fully reworked (such as Sanity, Status Cards, Torch, and more), and those broader changes are not listed here as simple bug fixes.[/i][/p][p][/p][h3][b]New Easy Difficulty Level[/b][/h3][p]A new [i]Newcomer[/i] difficulty setting has been added to make the game more approachable for players seeking a lighter challenge. This mode lowers survival demands (hunger, thirst, tiredness) and combat intensity, which should help you experience the Story Mode and explore the Survival Mode.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Sanity Rework [/b][/h3][p]The Sanity System was visually updated and expanded with late-game mechanics, offering clearer feedback and a greater impact on gameplay at higher Adaptation levels.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Status Card Rework[/b][/h3][p]Status cards were redesigned for clarity and now provide more information about the environment and wilderness events, making it easier to prepare for what’s coming in the wild.[/p][h3][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1394960/view/569255906735293427"][/dynamiclink][b]Torch Rework [/b][/h3][p]The torch was integrated into the new combat system and can now be used as a weapon. Controls are smoother, durability is better balanced, and now you can block with it. It is still primarily used as a tool to scare away wolves when lit, rather than as a brute force weapon.[/p][h3][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1394960/view/525343813853513095"][/dynamiclink][b]Crafting UI Rework[/b] [/h3][p]The crafting interface was redesigned with cleaner navigation, now providing players with more information about crafted items for a clearer experience and less waste. We've talked a little bit about it in our previous announcement, so you can freely check this one out here:[/p][h3][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1394960/view/525346984576421315"][/dynamiclink][/h3][h3][b]Trolley Damage Rework[/b][/h3][p]The Trolley breaking up mechanic was adjusted to provide balanced and fair damage mechanics.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Bear Event Rework[/b][/h3][p]We completely reworked the Bear Wilderness Event. Now, the interaction with it is more intuitive for the player. You can check [b]The Road to Survival Just Got Smoother [/b]announcement [/p][p][/p][h3][b]Graphic Improvements [/b][/h3][p]The resource graphics have been fully overhauled with updated models, textures, and a consistent PBR workflow, including redesigned animal models with improved fur and updated foliage and hard surface assets. The rendering system has been enhanced with extensive exposure adjustments, and alternative versions of resources have been added to match different biomes. Overall, existing content has been polished to meet the quality standards of a full release.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Performance Improvements[/b][/h3][p]High settings now run efficiently on RTX 2060 and higher graphics cards. Major optimization of memory consumption for improved stability and performance. Added support for FSR, TSR, and DLSS technologies for enhanced upscaling and performance. notes.title: It's time to give you an update on Winter Survival's development 👀
notes.notes:
[h1]Hey, survivors! ❄️[/h1]

Since many of you have been with us since day one, we want to stay transparent and give you a sneak peek into what’s been happening behind the scenes with Winter Survival. With that said, it’s high time for an update on what we’ve been working on over the past few months. Ready to hop on the trolley and see what’s ahead? Then, let’s get this trolley rollin’ 🔥

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/51ed9fb5fa092023f4b000ec45a734db052040de.jpg[/img]

[h2]What are we working on right now? 🤔[/h2]

[h3]ACT III for Story Mode 💥[/h3]

As some of you might already know, we’re currently [b]hard at work bringing ACT III of Winter Survival’s Story Mode to life[/b], which will mark the finale of Danny’s journey through the treacherous, dangerous, and relentless wilderness. Simultaneously, the release of ACT III means that Winter Survival [b]will leave Early Access[/b] and officially enter its 1.0 state.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/647f235d1ac080d2fed39ac1c29e85a856761e74.jpg[/img]

[h3]What about the Survival Mode? 🐻[/h3]

That’s a pretty damn good question. The release of ACT III also means that Survival Mode will be getting new features as well. This includes [b]another scenario[/b] to choose from, a [b]fresh chunk of map[/b] to uncover, and of course, brand-new mechanics and [b]flintastic features[/b] that I’m going to have as an ace up my sleeve 😮

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/c3118efd2f3b06a1cf133970052d071bf67771e9.jpg[/img]

[h2]Is that all you got? 😒[/h2]

Definitely not! We’re still actively looking at your suggestions via Steam reviews and discussions as well as on our Discord server. Thanks to your invaluable feedback, some of the features that didn’t meet your expectations — like the [b]torch rework, building system, and trolley damage mechanic[/b], to name a few — have already made their way into our internal testing branch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/7428a5ffed90d78a6a45ded97849704d864fe7a1.jpg[/img]

However, it’ll take some time to test them properly because we want to give you a product that’s as error-free as possible. Simply put: once we’re happy with the internal quality, that’s when the update will go live. Also, please keep in mind that if you’ve played Winter Survival recently, you might not have seen these changes reflected in gameplay just yet.

[h2]What’s next? ⏭️[/h2]

Now, it’s time to talk a little about how we plan to keep you more regularly updated on Winter Survival’s progress over the coming months. First and foremost, we’re planning to [b]bring back regular development updates[/b] here on Steam. Personally, I’ve always enjoyed creating these kinds of materials, and based on your responses before Winter Survival launched, it seemed like you did too. We’ll be combining that renewed communication with [b]themed months, starting in June, when we’ll focus on Story Mode[/b] and how development is shaping up.

Apart from that, I highly encourage you to join our [url=https://discord.gg/dragoent]official Discord server[/url] and follow our social media accounts. There’s going to be a lot happening soon — [b]AMAs, Dev Talks, Q&A sessions[/b], just to name a few. And hey, don’t hesitate to leave a comment below if you have any suggestions on how you’d prefer us to communicate with you.

[url=https://discord.gg/dragoent][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/3ede1d0db091e3d8b2f8267158423474ad668cfb.gif[/img][/url]

[h2]Stay up-to-date 📰[/h2]

And that’s it for today’s announcement! As always, if you have any suggestions, ideas, or problems, make sure to leave a comment below. I believe the next announcement should go live by the end of May, so if you don’t want to miss that, be sure to follow Winter Survival on Steam and our social channels. Can’t wait to hear your thoughts — but for now, stay sane and don’t let those pesky wolves catch you. Until the next devlog! 👋

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1394960/Winter_Survival/

[i]~ Sewek[/i]

notes.title: Hotfix #2 for Winter Survival ACTII is here.
notes.notes:
[h1]New & Improved[/h1]

- Added voice line for starting Panic Attack
- Added Trap tutorial near the Rabbit Quest (Traps are single use at the moment. After it's used or broken by an animal you can loot it for extra resources but can not pick it up again. We are considering this to be changed in the future.)

[h2]Balance[/h2]
We rebalanced the Weather System:
- There should no longer be situations where multiple weather areas overlap causing extreme drop in temperature in a small area.

[h3]For Story:[/h3]
- Act 1 location ambient temperature is set to -10 (-8 for the first night), 
- Act 2 locations are set to -13. Of course, different weathers add to ambient temperature,
- Cloudy weather can appear after the first night
- Snowy weather can appear after "The Survival Instinct" quest (Rabbit Hunting)
- Snowy and windy weather can appear after the "Hunting" quest (Deer Hunting Act 2)
- Blizzard weather can appear after picking up the lever from "Echoes of Sabotage II"

[h3]For Survival:[/h3]
- Every area is set to -10 with all weathers possible from the start.

[h3]For Story and Survival:[/h3]
- Area 3 (Mountain in Act 2) - always blizzard, and near the mountain, there is always snow
- Area 6 (Behind the Act 2 final gate) - Possible weather is snowy, snowy and windy or blizzard (temp. Story -13 for Endless -10)
- Shelter buff now gives an additional 5 cold protection (was 10)
- Cave buff now gives an additional 2 cold protection (was 6) but retains the coldness from the weather outside, so in net it will now usually be a bit colder in caves.
- Hot springs now give +10 to ambient temperature (was +15) and in addition, increase the wetness by +4

[h3]Campfire changes to ambient temperature:[/h3]
- Basic campfire gives +8 
- A proper campfire gives +10
- Platform campfire gives +13
- Long campfire gives +14
- Tepee campfire gives + 18
- Shelter campfires +13 (also campfires in hunters' and woodcutters' huts in Story)

[h3]Weather changes to ambient temperature and wetness:[/h3]
- Clear weather is from 0 to -2 (was 0 to -1), for wetness it is -1 (was -2 to -4)
- Cloudy weather is from -2.5 to -3.5 (was -2 to -3), wetness 1
- Snowy weather is from -4 to -6 (was -3 to -4), wetness from 2 to 4
- Snowy and windy weather is from -5 to -7 (was -5 to -6), wetness from 4 to 6 
- Blizzard stays -8, wetness 8

- Main heat multiplier increased by 20% (will be getting cold and warm 20% faster)

[h3]Story Specific:[/h3]
- Switched equipment to a Small Spear Holder at the beginning of Act 2
- Added Bone Axe schematic to Hunting Book but removed it from the start of Act 2
- Moved the Bone Axe to Act 2 to avoid sidetracking progress

[h3]Cold Wave:[/h3]
- We changed the MMR calculation to add bonus points for Survival Time
- Changed duration of the Cold Wave Gold beams to make them easier to spot

[h3]Events:[/h3]
- Cargo Drop Event frequency increased [now it happens randomly 1-3 days instead of 5 days]
- Relocated one of the Wolf Aftermath Event near the green lever
- Relocated one of Wolf Aftermath Event on Rabbit Glade further from the Bonfire
- Relocated one of the Wolf Aftermath Event near the Paratrooper

[h3]Other:[/h3]

notes.title: Winter Survival – ACT II Release Date Announcement🔥
notes.notes:
[h1]Hey, survivors! ❄️[/h1]

Your favorite marketing guy strikes again! This time, I thought it'd be great to share what the future holds for us in the upcoming weeks. Before I’ll dive into the nitty-gritty details, I’d like to thank each and every one of you who shared your ideas, suggestions, and general feedback with us. Whether it’s been on the discussion forum, our discord, or under the announcements – you guys helped us make the game better, and we’re so thankful for that. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/aaf017618e1680c7b640f4ac3ef5fbd9d75e9ae2.jpg[/img]

Now, let’s get back to the details, shall we? Many of you have been asking about the next content update for Winter Survival especially related to its story. And this devlog is gonna be all about it – I’ll try to give you as much details as possible without any spoilers, so grab your favorite drink and snack, and let’s roll! 

[h2]ACT II Releases in the end of July🔥[/h2]

That's right! Many of you have been asking about when the next update is gonna be available. I'm more than thrilled to say that you're gonna be able to continue your journey on [b]July 24th, 2024[/b]. How cool is that? Now, let's check the brand-new teaser for ACT II – spoiler alert – gameplay showcase is coming next week, so stay tuned for more💪

[previewyoutube=HBGtkbEWUYs;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]What’s gonna be my main goal?[/h2]

Your main goal in Act II will be to reach a Harbour. As simple as it sounds it won’t be an easy task, and you will need to complete several different quests in order to reach your final destination. Act II will also be the time when you’ll have to face multiple situations in which you’ll have to decide not only your fate but maybe, just maybe, the fate of the others. I don’t want to spill the beans too early, so you have to wait until ACT II releases!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/55f6834caf1d185d872b1f5465477f0de3d7d253.jpg[/img]

[h2]Everything must come to an end😢[/h2]

And that’s it for our today's announcement. I’m dying to know what you guys think about it, so the comment section below belongs to you right now. Please keep in mind that Act II is not the only thing that we’re working on right now. While we understand that many of you have been eagerly waiting for the next part of the story, we’re still working on bringing you Coldwave mode which we’ve announced a while back ago, so keep an eye out for that as well. A little birdie told me that you can expect some news regarding Cold Wave next week, so stay tuned for more information. Until the next devlog!

notes.title: Game Update #10 - Combat and Trolley Rework
notes.notes:
[h2]New & Improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] The Combat System has been reworked to offer a smoother and more dynamic experience when fighting using a spear. We also tweaked a lot of the damage values to be in-line with all these changes (see Balance section). 
[list]
[*] [b]Block[/b] has been added to combat allowing you to block attacks and mitigate damage. Blocking drains stamina. By default, hold the Right Mouse Button to block. 
[*] With the addition of Block, the [b]Throw[/b] mechanic has been tweaked, too. Use the V key to change to throwing and charge the throw with the Left Mouse Button as before. If you don’t like V as the key to do so, please remap it to a key of your liking in the Options.
[*] We got rid of the disorienting animation when impaling.
[*] Impaling can now [b]stun[/b] a target and the stunned state is now shown with a new Stunned marker on the animal. Dealing damage to the animal interrupts the stun.
[*] Wolves regained the ability to make the player [b]bleed[/b] with a bite attack!
[*] 15% change to apply a bleed effect with bite attack and 10% with knockdown on Survivalist difficulty.
[*] 10% change to apply a bleed effect with bite attack and 5% with knockdown on Explorer difficulty.
[/list][/list][list]
[*] Trolley has seen various improvements. Apart from various smaller fixes and tweaks, we reworked the Trolley Switches and Levers. You now [b]need a lever[/b] in order to activate a rail switch. Your previous switch settings have been reset with this update. Don’t worry though, you’ll find the levers close to the corresponding switch. The switches also have new visuals and they now show the direction they have been switched to.
[list]
[*] Trolley Torch Holder Upgrade - we added an additional upgrade to the Trolley, now you’ll have a source of light to ride through tunnels and in the night without the need to drain batteries on your flashlight..
[*] Trolley Storage Chest - another upgrade for the Trolley allowing you to have a mobile storage with [b]600 storage capacity[/b]. 
[*] Both upgrades are available in the Trolley Upgrade station in Endless mode upon reaching Adaptation level 25.
[/list]
[*] Compass and Compass Markers - now you can use compass markers to navigate around the environment. In Endless mode you can find the compass hidden in the environment, but in Story mode you’ll get it along with your other equipment in the backpack. Recipes for Compass Marker are available on Adaptation level 10 in Endless mode and immediately after finding the Compass in the Story. 
Wooden and Stone Markers can be crafted, so no matter where you are, the necessary resources should be easily available. Interact with the crafted and placed Compass Markers to select icons and colors that will indicate this location on your compass and make your navigation easier.
[*] Foxes - we added a new inhabitant to the Fox Glade which is the area in Endless that you can find behind a Trolley Gate. It may be hard to hunt it with a spear, but try to use the newly added Fox Snack to lure it into a trap. The Fox Snack is craftable on Adaptation level 9 in Endless mode.
[*] Added a schematic for a small Spear Holder and plugged it into the ending of False Dawn quest as well as first pickup of the item. Just in case you somehow manage to lose your basic spear holder.
[*] Added a schematic for a Stone Basket to the Adaptation System at Level 14 in Endless mode. As the name suggests, it allows you to store stones like the branch holders allow you to store branches.
[*] Empty alcohol bottles, wild flowers, broken boar tusks, leaky cans, old needles and rabbit feet made stackable.
[*] Improved the movement of the deer so it gets stuck less often in various world objects.

[/list]

notes.title: Game Update #5 is here!

[h2]Game Update #5 (v12398)[/h2]
Unstuck feature and some important bug fixes along with further balancing changes/improvements.
And we will go with normal update numbers going forward as nobody could remember the long build numbers anyway :P

[h2]New[/h2]
[list]
[*] Loot window now closes automatically when you press "Take All".
[*] "Unstuck" feature has been added to the In-game Menu. Its purpose is to free you when you get stuck somewhere and can't get out. It moves you to the nearest "safe location". Unstuck is not usable in combat. 
This is still [b]EXPERIMENTAL[/b]. It is[b] NOT intended for Story mode[/b] - while it could "unstuck" your character, it might break a story related quest or progression. A later update will make Unstuck compatible with Story mode.
This feature is intended for Endless mode at this time, since players gained access to areas of the game world we haven't really intended for them to get access to just yet. Unlike Story mode, the game world in Endless is a lot larger and still changing, so there is risk of places where players might get stuck and unable to get out on their own. 
[/list]

[*] Increased durability of Bone Knife, Stone Spear and Bone Spear. As these items are made from better materials and require a workbench to be crafted, they should last longer than their basic counterparts.

Today, I’d like to announce that we’ve already implemented most of your feedback into the demo. This means easier wolves on explorer difficulty, improved tutorial system, more hiding bushes and healing materials, and so on. Full patch notes are available down below 👇

notes.title: Winter Survival Development Update #16 – Advanced Mechanics part 2🐺
notes.notes:
[h1]Hey, survivors![/h1]

Welcome back to another exciting devlog for Winter Survival. As we continue to shape our frozen wilderness, I’m thrilled to invite you to join me on a jaw-dropping adventure, where I’m gonna be sharing another part of our advanced mechanics series. If you somehow missed the first part, you can still check it out right now by clicking this link. In today’s devlog, I’ll delve into some intricate interactions with the local fauna, highlighting the intelligence and unpredictability of the animals that roam our wintry landscapes. Without further ado, let’s jump straight into the devlog. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/72aad1036448bd1cbfdcf9e4f9419d7b2cfb4270.png[/img]

[h2]Advanced Mechanics 🧠[/h2]

[h3]Wolf Party 🐺[/h3]

One of the most intriguing dynamics in Winter Survival is the emergence of wolf parties. Picture this: as you navigate the snow-covered environment, you may stumble upon a group of wolves feasting on a fresh carcass. These wolf parties add a layer of unpredictability to your survival journey. Now it’s for you to decide, because it’s a high risk but high reward thing – if you have a torch, you can always try to fend them off and take what’s left from the carcass. Whether you’re gonna be successful or not by doing so depends on your survival skills and how well you’re prepared. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/e8390f0c814c70f1294116b29a6c9a42258fb0ca.gif[/img]

[h3]Wounded Animal 🦌[/h3]

Another awe-inspiring feature that our team has implemented is the wounded animal as we like to call it. Just like in real world, the environment reacts to certain activities that we do on a daily basis. In Winter Survival it's basically the same case. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/1d81fe3d49508c3f011b0d6bf988c19dbab85d2d.gif[/img]

If you happen to trap and hurt a deer, you have a small window of opportunity to hunt it down and take as much as you can. You never know if there aren't any wolves nearby.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/06c0febaff6ffbf5338b5cf96dd335f609623bbd.gif[/img]

[h3]Bear Rampage 🐻[/h3]

Surviving the winter isn't just about battling the elements and hunger; it's also about navigating the animal threats, especially the bear. In Winter Survival, we've introduced a heavily impactful mechanic where our dreaded nemesis can inadvertently destroy player-built shelters. 

Let me give you an example – let’s assume that you’re going out into the wilderness in search of supplies, crafting materials, or just to explore the surrounding area. By the time you come back you might find that your cozy shelter is partially destroyed. Now the question is – Are you gonna risk your life and stay in the area? Or maybe you decide to leave this place and your belongings behind for a while and come back as soon as you feel like the area is secured? Let me tell ya – I’d make the decision sooner rather than later, because our furry friend might be back in the blink of an eye. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/5c90ff373d153093d0ac1f73424dca7410cacbd3.jpg[/img]

[h2]Stay up-to-date 📰[/h2]

As we wrap up this devlog, we're thrilled to showcase the depth and complexity of Winter Survival's game world. The wolf parties, wolf howls, and bear rampages are just a glimpse into the intricate tapestry we're weaving for players. Every playthrough promises a fresh set of challenges and surprises, thanks to the advanced mechanics that make our world truly dynamic and alive.

Before we finish, I’d also like to mention that our friends over at Pyramid Games would like to invite you to check what they’ve been cooking up for their jaw-dropping, set on a Mars survival game - Occupy Mars. The best thing though – the game is currently on sale, so if you’re looking for scientific-oriented survival game, or maybe you’d like to give it to someone special, Occupy Mars will definitely meet your expectations

https://store.steampowered.com/app/758690/Occupy_Mars_The_Game/

And that’s gonna be it for today! Stay tuned for more updates as we continue to refine and expand Winter Survival. I can't wait for you to experience the peril and beauty of our frozen realm. Until next time, stay warm, stay vigilant, and may your survival instincts guide you through the winter's unforgiving embrace. Until the next devlog! 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1394960/Winter_Survival/

[i]~Your humble marketing guy - Sewek[/i]

notes.title: Winter Survival Development Update #15 – Advanced Mechanics part 1 ⚒️
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/310f49a9a27e2847f16198746c8e902597b49744.jpg[/img]
[h1]Hey, survivors! ❄️[/h1]

Welcome to another Winter Survival’s development update. In our recent announcement I’ve delved deeper into everything bear-related, so if you haven’t read it yet, you can freely do so by clicking [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1394960/view/6738003788162098620]this link[/url]. 

So, what do I have for you today? In today’s devlog we’re gonna dive into more advanced game mechanics – some of those are connected strictly to survival, and some exist to show you the effects of your actions to stay alive, often at any cost. Grab your favorite drink, prepare some snacks, and let’s roll! 

[h2]Sleeping outside 🛌[/h2]

Let’s start with the simplest yet most common mechanic – sleeping outside. In most survival games what you’d normally do is to build a basic shelter where you can sleep and save your progress. Then you’d venture deeper into the world in search of the perfect spot on the map where you’d start building your dream base a.k.a. recreating Minas Tirith or something else. 

In Winter Survival it’s “just” a little bit different – technically you can sleep outside. However, it can lead to some unexpected consequences. First one being the drop of your body temperature assuming that you didn’t make a fire. Even if you did take care of that, there is another thing – unforeseen wolf encounters, as I like to call it. If you have a torch at hand or even a spear then you might be able to fend them off, but if not… Then let me tell ya – the future doesn’t seem so bright for you. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/b67124eb789c0abb010dc6ab1820f14e9c8351d1.gif[/img]

[h2]Cooking outside 🍖[/h2]

“I’m starving, so I’m just gonna make a campfire and cook some delicious meat that I stole from the unexpected nightly pack of wolves. It won’t take that much time, so soon my stomach is gonna be full, and I’ll be ready for another day” – thought one already dead survivalist. 

In other words – I highly advise you to think twice before you’ll make the choice to cook outside as the smell will attract wild animals. If you’re lucky enough you’ll encounter a boar, but what if that’s gonna be a bear? Let me give you some advice – cooking outside is a last resort, and you’ll need to think twice before you make the decision. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/654a9b76d96261050426e764a01d1f5a4238e279.gif[/img]

[h2]Stench 🦨[/h2]

Just like in real life, doing certain actions will make your character sweat, which will lead to you building up quite a stench. But how is that supposed to be a problem? You might think. Well, the answer is simple – animal noses are far more sensitive than our human ones. Hunting will become a problem as the animals will smell you from a mile away. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/98c5e80f20fca153f6bc625cff8a4e58e42f550e.gif[/img]

As you can see, hunting takes time and proper preparation, so if you want to avoid being spotted before you even notice your prey, washing yourself before will do the trick. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/f5e7296ec5eac58f22c720e1355e5916fe819c36.gif[/img]

[h2]Cargo 📦[/h2]

Surprise, surprise… It’s a special delivery time. From time to time, a plane will drop a cargo box in a random place on the map. The box will contain some high-value resources, so it’s definitely something worth venturing out for. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/2ff3244ef6ac57ec46d64ef7361097add6c1d64a.jpg[/img]

However, it won’t be that easy. Not only will the cargo drop in the evening, when there’s gonna be a bunch of wild animals lurking in the shadows, but also you’ll have a limited time to get the resources you want. To find the exact location of a cargo, you’re gonna need to use your walkie-talkie. Think of it as a hot & cold game – the closer you’ll get to the cargo location, the stronger the signal will be from the walkie-talkie. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/4daa6012e6e4c38ad8988e4d76a526a6e93c985e.gif[/img]

[h2]Stay up-to-date 📰[/h2]

And this is how this devlog comes to an end. What do you think about some of the advanced mechanics that you will encounter in the game? Did you enjoy today’s devlog? Make sure to let us know in the comments below. However, please do keep in mind that it's still work-in-progress stuff, so some things that you've witnessed here might differ from the final product. Last but not the least, if you don’t want to miss the next devlog or any other news regarding Winter Survival, consider adding the game to your wishlist 🙇

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1394960/Winter_Survival/

[i]~Your humble marketing guy – Sewek[/i]

The Prologue will be available for you to try on [b]February 6th, 2023, as a part of the upcoming Steam Next Fest event[/b]. We hope that you’re as excited as we’re right now, and we cannot wait to see what your experience with the Prologue is. 

What is more, we’re constantly gathering feedback regarding the current stage of the game, so as soon as the Prologue is live, feel free to send it to us so we can prepare the game for the Early Access release even better. 

Key features of the Winter Survival: Prologue:

[*] A unique sanity system – you’re just a regular person - wild animals and darkness scare you. Push yourself too hard, don’t sleep enough, and bad things will happen… Want to survive, free from insanity? Learn to take better care of yourself. Or maybe you’re looking for a challenge? Let the madness inside then and let it rule your mind. See how far you can go before you break.
[*] Stealth is your best friend –  every animal has a range of hearing and sight, so pay attention to stay out of their way. Here, you are the prey, and the best thing you can do is avoid everything that wants to eat you. 
[*] Expect the unexpected – The winter will chill you to the bone. So do everything you can to survive on your long and cold journey home. This is nature at its deadliest – the culmination of its forces against you.
[*] The Wilderness – remember that during your journey back home, you will encounter a variety of different animals. Some of them are harmless, but some will do everything to tear you apart.

notes.title: Demo Patch #1
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/0e0e181aa9e20c03d3534edeb72fda88055dbaaf.jpg[/img]

The first patch for the demo of Winter Survival Simulator with a series of bug fixes and improvements (0.9.3)

[b]Quality of Life Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fuel slot added to cooking items in case you wanted to Drag & Drop instead of Right Clicking the fuel items.
[*] UI fonts have been rescaled to make them a bit more readable on average screen setup.
[*] Heat Slider added to Heat in Instinct Mode to make it clearer on what our heat level is at when instinct mode is enabled.
[*] We added a slider for Camera Bob through Gameplay Options (Idle Animations etc.) in case it's causing motion sickness.
[*] We added an option disabling of Mouse Rotation Lag through Gameplay Options.
[*] We added an option to enable / disable Motion Blur through Gameplay Options.
[*] We allow disabling of Backpack Animations through Gameplay Options to help with motion sickness.
[*] We added an option to change mouse sensitivity and inversion of mouse on X/Y axis.
[*] More keys added to keybindings options to allow further customization.
[/list]
[b]Gameplay[/b]
[list]
[*] Canteen now visually shows on the slot background whether it's holding Geyser Water or Icy Water once filled.
[*] Geyser Water now correctly warms you up slightly while hurting you for drinking it.
[*] Instinct Mode had its visuals updated slightly and now slows down time while used by roughly 15%
[*] Bear tracks reworked to feel a little less magical and a bit more, grounded.
[*] We no longer allow dropping of 'important quest items' from the inventory! No more throwing of trap parts and canteens off the bridge.
[*] We added more heat on 'Find the Heat Source' objective completion to prevent an edge case where your hands would stay frozen if you left the hot springs area too quickly.
[*] Speeded up axe animations to make cutting down trees a bit more responsive.
[*] Backpack can now be picked up even if your inventory is full without dropping the item.
[*] 
[/list]
[b]UI[/b]
[list]
[*] All sounds sliders should now be working correctly.
[*] Visual added when trying to drop items.
[/list]
[b]Sounds[/b]
[list]
[*] Body movement sounds will now stop when tutorial is on.
[*] Few extra sound effects added and tweaked some of the repetitive sound effects to be less annoying. (Crows etc.)
[/list]
[b]Game Balance[/b]
[list]
[*] You will no longer get hungry quite as quickly. (About 15% slower)
[*] You will not longer get thirsty quite as quickly. (About 7% slower)
[*] All food items now feel a bit more filling. (You no longer need to eat 8 rabbits to feel like you're not starving.)
[/list]
[b]AI[/b]
[list]
[*] Minor adjustments to wolves to make them a bit 'smarter' for players who were avoiding wolves by jumping on the rocks.
[/list]

[b]Upcoming Changes[/b]
[list]
[*] Checkpoint System / Number of Checkpoints will be increased, and options to load checkpoint from Main Menu will be allowed.
[*] In some cases you can see items in Instinct Mode on a very large distance (Renders through Foliage at any distance).
[*] Keybind rebinding to 'same' key in multiple categories is still not supported - occasionally leads to some funky things when rebinding keys.
[*] Stats / Instinct Mode are not split yet on separate keybinding.
[*] Instinct Mode doesn't drain energy.
[*] If you do Shelter Repairs without having Instinct Mode enabled, the repairs don't show up until you toggle instinct mode.
[*] Cold / Freezing doesn't quite affect you as strongly as we would like.
[/list]
